subject: mixed multi-logit model: optimization and log-likelihood for WAIC

messages.author: b278d86c3552dc73
messages.subject: mixed multi-logit model: optimization and log-likelihood for WAIC
parts:
Update: I've attached a file with a revised and working code of the model, in case someone needs it.

****************************
Original message:

Dear Stanners,

thanks a lot to the developers of this amazing software. I've just fit my first model in RStan, and it seems to be working! It's a multi-logit model that predicts the use of three semantically similar verbs, let, allow and permit, based on several contextual variables from the British National Corpus. The random intercepts are the infinitives that follow these verbs and the corpus files the occurrences of the letting verbs are extracted from. The results (the fixed effects) are very similar to my previous mlogit and MCMCglmm models. Since it's a quite rare type of models, I have two questions:

1) Is the code I use to compute the log-likelihood values correct? I need it to compute WAIC. I can't find examples for multi-logit models, unfortunately.

generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (n in 1:N){
    log_lik[n] <- categorical_logit_log(y[n], col(y_hat, n));
}


2) I'm not very happy about the use of col(), as above, and indexing the rows and columns in a matrix, as below, but I haven't been able to find a better solution so far. Is there a way to make the code more efficient?

  for (n in 1:N){
   for (k in 2:K)
    y_hat[k, n] <- alpha[k] + beta[k]*x[n] + v[k, verbs[n]] + f[k, files[n]];
}


I would be very grateful for any tips and hints! 


All the best,
Natalia


Here's the full model:

optimize_model <-  'data {
  int<lower=2> K;             // num categorical outcomes (let, allow or permit) 
  int<lower=1> D;             // num fixed effects (without intercept) 
  int<lower=0> N;             // num observations 
  vector[D] x[N];              // fixed effects 
  int<lower=1,upper=K> y[N];  // response with categorical outcomes
  int<lower=1> V; //number of verbs (infinitives) - random intercepts
  int<lower=1> F; //number of corpus files - random intercepts
  int<lower=1, upper=V> verbs[N]; //verb id - random intercepts
  int<lower=1, upper=F> files[N]; //corpus file id - random intercepts
} 


parameters { 
  vector[K-1] alpha_raw;          // intercepts 
  matrix[K-1, D] beta_raw;     // slopes of fixed effects
  matrix[K-1,V] v_raw; //random intercepts (verbs)
  matrix[K-1,F] f_raw; //random intercepts (files)
  real<lower=0> sigma_v; //random intercepts (verbs)
  real<lower=0> sigma_f; ////random intercepts (files)
} 

transformed parameters {
  vector[K] alpha;
  matrix[K, D] beta;
  matrix[K, V] v;
  matrix[K, F] f;
  matrix[K, N] y_hat;
  alpha[1] <- 0;
  for (k in 2:K)
        alpha[k] <- alpha_raw[k-1];
  beta <- append_row(rep_row_vector(0, D), beta_raw);
  for (k in 2:K) {
        v[k] <- v_raw[k-1];
        f[k] <- f_raw[k-1];
  }
  v <- append_row(rep_row_vector(0, V), v_raw);
  f <- append_row(rep_row_vector(0, F), f_raw);
  for (n in 1:N){
   for (k in 2:K)
    y_hat[k, n] <- alpha[k] + beta[k]*x[n] + v[k, verbs[n]] + f[k, files[n]];
}
}

model { 
  // priors 
  alpha_raw ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  for (k in 1:K-1){
  beta_raw[k] ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
  v_raw[k] ~ normal(0, sigma_v);
  f_raw[k] ~ normal(0, sigma_f); 
  }
  // likelihood 
  for (n in 1:N)
    y[n] ~ categorical_logit(alpha + beta*x[n] + col(v, verbs[n]) + col(f, files[n])); 
}

generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (n in 1:N){
    log_lik[n] <- categorical_logit_log(y[n], col(y_hat, n));
}
}
'

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: mixed multi-logit model: optimization and log-likelihood for WAIC
parts: 1) Is the code I use to compute the log-likelihood values correct? I need it to compute WAIC. I can't find examples for multi-logit models, unfortunately.

Instead of WAIC, we recommend to compute LOO-CV with Pareto Smoothed Importance Sampling 
 - Aki Vehtari, Andrew Gelman and Jonah Gabry (2015). Efficient implementation of leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC for evaluating fitted Bayesian models. arXiv preprint arXiv:1507.04544. http://arxiv.org/abs/1507.04544
as it is more reliable and easier to check the quality of the estimate (both IS-LOO and WAIC may give overoptimistic predictive performance estimates, see the paper for more information.)

When you compute the likelihood in model block (or actually log likelihood, although the current notation hides it), you have

// likelihood 
  for (n in 1:N)
    y[n] ~ categorical_logit(alpha + beta*x[n] + col(v, verbs[n]) + col(f, files[n])); 
}
So when you compute the log likelihood in generated quantities, you should have

log_lik[n] <- categorical_logit_log(y[n], alpha + beta*x[n] + col(v, verbs[n]) + col(f, files[n]));

I'm not sure if  col(y_hat, n) gives you the same result?

Aki
